case_title: Yashodhan Singh & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.147, 148, 149, 302, 452, 307, 504 (as registered in the FIR)
evidence_type: Complainant's evidence (basis of s.319 application); other evidence not stated
trial_court_outcome: Summoned the appellants under s.319 Cr.P.C. to join the trial as accused
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed; summoning order affirmed
neutral_facts: An FIR was registered at a police station in Hathras on 9 June 2018, based on a complaint by the complainant concerning an incident at the complainant's house. The complaint alleged that a group of persons, later identified as the accused, went to the house, began hurling abuses, and opened fire. The complainant sustained injuries, and two of the complainant's brothers died. The FIR recorded offences of rioting, rioting with a deadly weapon, unlawful assembly with a common object, murder, house-trespass, attempt to murder and intentional insult. Investigation followed and a charge sheet was filed against the persons named in the FIR. The persons later sought to be added as accused were not mentioned in that charge sheet, because their role was still under investigation.
physical_harm: As alleged in the FIR: injuries to the complainant and the death of two of the complainant's brothers
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR registered 09.06.2018); trial judgment: not given (summoning order 23.09.2022); High Court: 03.01.2023; Supreme Court: 18.07.2023
legal_representation: Appellants: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv. (with others). State: Ratnakar Dash, Sr. Adv. (with others). Complainant: Yatharth Singh (counsel)
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed against named accused; appellants not named in it as their role was under investigation
appeal_history: Trial court: summoned appellants under s.319 (23.09.2022). High Court: revision dismissed (03.01.2023). Supreme Court: appeal dismissed (18.07.2023)
prosecution_argument: State and complainant argued that the Jogendra Yadav observations on prior hearing are fact-specific; a pre-summoning hearing would create a trial within a trial, delay the trial and affect speedy trial under Article 21; s.319 is to be invoked on the evidence and satisfaction of the trial court under Hardeep Singh
defence_argument: Summoned persons must be heard before being added as accused, relying on para 9 of Jogendra Yadav; alternatively the matter should go to a larger Bench; a discharge application should be available
legal_principle_applied: No pre-summoning hearing is required under s.319 Cr.P.C.; a summoned person cannot seek discharge under s.227; para 9 of Jogendra Yadav is not ratio and is confined to its facts; the satisfaction required is higher than that for framing charge
precedent_relied_upon: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab (2014) 3 SCC 92 (followed); Sukhpal Singh Khair v. State of Punjab (2023) 1 SCC 289 (followed); Brijendra Singh v. State of Rajasthan (2017) 7 SCC 706 (followed); Jogendra Yadav v. State of Bihar (2015) 9 SCC 244 (not to be reconsidered; para 9 relatable only to its facts)
